text:
Alex: FYI — got a KV-cache OOM on prod-host-22 during a long-context load test. stack traces look like heavy reuse + paging churn.

Priya: ugh. which workload? long-chat or batched-embed?

Alex: Long-chat stress test, ~120k token session. Kernel selector switched to fast-atten-quant at 11:02 which increased per-token KV footprint.

Jorge: any dump/heap profile?

Alex: uploaded a pprof here: s3://redwood-perf/4071234567/profiles/kv-heap-11-02.pb.gz. top lines show many small slab allocations around slabmap::reuse_window.

Maya: that kernel change was rolled a few hours earlier in the canary rollout. Might be a kernel memory regression.

Priya: do we see fragmentation + total committed growth, or just higher live allocations?

Alex: both. resident set grew steadily, and fragmentation ratio jumped ~1.9x in the 30m before OOM. paging rate spiked too.

Jorge: hypothesis: kernel toggled a path that avoids sharing KV pages (for speed) but allocates pinned buffers. Combined with our batching heuristic, many parallel sessions kept distinct reuse windows in GPU memory.

Maya: that matches the timeline. Also saw increased micro-batches per request due to a heuristic tweak for batching latency. More micro-batches -> more KV copies in-flight.

Priya: quick mitigations to push now?

Alex: proposed hotfix: force kernel to legacy-kv-share path for models >= 8k context on Hosted pool A. Also reduce max micro-batches from 8 -> 4 for long-context routes.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: rollback kernel selector on canary (deploy-1234). ETA 6m.

Jorge: also enable aggressive soft-evict: kv.evict_aggressive=true and kv.max_reuse_window=256 for affected hosts, so we reclaim earlier.

Maya: watchouts: aggressive evict may worsen latency tail for really large dialogues. We should gate by request length.

Priya: agree. Do a rule: if ctx_len > 32k then prefer fallback model-mini-quant with smaller KV size and return header X-REDWOOD-FALLBACK.

Alex: added a short-lived metric: kv_reuse_window_count and kv_eviction_rate to the perf dashboard. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood/perf/d/kv-oom-4071234567

Jorge: good. let's also add an automatic canary guard: if host_resident_growth_rate > 5%/min during canary, abort rollout and rollback kernel automatically.

Maya: I'll open a PR for the kernel selector rollback + batching cap. Priya, can you own the fallback rule and dashboard panels?

Priya: on it. I'll also create an eval job to compare quality of fallback model-mini-quant vs main on our regression prompts.

infra-bot: deploy succeeded: rollback applied to canary hosts (deploy-1234) at 11:15.

Alex: after rollback, host-22 resident growth flattened and no OOMs in the next 40m. Preliminary: rollback fixed the leak/regression.

Jorge: next steps: postmortem with kernel change diff, batching tweak, and telemetry gaps. We need finer-grained KV metrics (per-session reuse window bytes + pinned-page count).

Maya: agree. Also propose a new graceful-degrade flow: detect rising kv_eviction_rate -> throttle batching -> fallback model -> soft-reject new long sessions when host is > 85% mem.

Priya: added follow-up tasks in the incident board: 1) revert kernel change permanently until perf-sig review, 2) add per-session KV telemetry, 3) prod guardrails for canary.

Alex: thanks team. I'll stitch logs + heap profiles into the postmortem doc and ping on all-hands. :bow:

Maya: nice work catching this quickly.

Priya: I'll upload the eval results and quality diffs later today.

Jorge: tagging this for eng-runtime retrospective.

infra-bot: incident closed (no active regressions) at 11:55.
